newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down, fail to crack 9,600 level.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down, fail to crack 9,600 level.

text.p: Taiwan's stock index once again failed to crack the 9,600-point resistance, losing steam from early gains to close lower on Wednesday as bellwether electronics were unable to carry the market, brokers said.
Brokers nevertheless said they expected the index to glide pass the 9,600 level in the near term as other weak counters should be able to rise again after falling for several days.
The benchmark stock index, which soared to an intraday high 9,648.43, lost momentum in the final hour of trade to close a scant 11.42 points or 0.12 percent lower at 9,544.56.
Turnover was a hectic T$258.8 billion, second only to Tuesday's all-time high of T$262 billion.
The board index has been testing the 9,600 level since Monday, but failed to stand above the level amid strong technical and psychological pressure, brokers said.

"The electronics were the only sector to carry the market, and there was no way they could hold the bourse when other sectors dropped sharply," United Securities' Lin Long-hsien said. He said the continued electronic bull run has absorbed investment funds which would have been pegged at other stocks, thus resulting in the fall of most other share prices.
Major sectors, including plastics, textile and construction, fell sharply. Construction was the worst hit, losing 4.7 percent, while plastics also dipped 4.27 percent.
Electronics rose 4.53 percent on heavy buying. Many electronic shares, boosted by expectations of sound sales growth, had risen to the daily seven percent limit.

Notebook computer maker Inventec Corp, one of several high-tech firms to report strong commercial orders, was up T$13 to T$199. Motherboard giant Asustek had risen T$32 to T$495, while mircochip giant Taiwan Semiconductor was up T$9.5 to T$149.
"The electronics bull run also reflects the upswing in Wall Street," Virginia Tsai of National Securities said.
Wall Street stocks finished broadly higher on Tuesday.
Brokers said the strong electronics trend was not shaken by repeated central bank's market-cooling moves.
The bank repeatedly has issued negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess funds in the market, apparently hoping to slow the flow of funds into the bourse.
"Other industrial sectors have been losing for several days, and should be able to recover on Thursday," Lin said.
A 9,560-9,650 range was seen for Thursday.
